source_pages: printed p.228-231 / PDF 230-233, read whole and verified against 170-dpi renders 2026-08-23
family_naming_note: Namespaced 'Wall H.72' for the same reason as the other wall families: the registry merges section files by family NAME and the catalog uses 'H. 72' for more than one thing.
extraction_note: Nine of twelve positions, 27 of 31 codes. LEFT OUT: the 90-degree corner (OE0713 / OE0715), the straight corner (PE094D/S) - both Elda Q7b - and the microwave-niche unit PE0696, which is NOT 720 tall and therefore not a member of this family at all; it has its own file, wall_h72_microwave_niche.json. See page_observations.
letter_note: PE = H.72 was read on printed p.228 on 2026-08-18, before this extraction. The filler table on printed p.434 agrees.

data.mounting_note: Catalog-level fact: every unit in the wall chapter hangs. HOW HIGH is a project decision and lives in Standards::WALL_MOUNT_BOTTOM_MM until M1.6.
data.n_elle_note: The elevation carries 'N Elle' at 74,2 = 72 + 2,2, the same +22 mm as every other wall family. RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED. CORRECTION 2026-08-23, evening (rule 9 - added, not erased): THIS FIGURE IS NOT PRINTED ON THE PAGE. pdftotext -bbox puts 'N- Elle' at a normal 7,5 pt over the perspective drawing on every wall page of this chapter; rendering exactly that box at 400 and at 600 dpi shows blank paper. It is white text, or a hidden layer for the N_Elle edition - IN THE FILE, NOT IN THE BOOK. The wording above ('the elevation carries', 'the second elevation on this page') is therefore wrong, and the H.48 note's guess that the 170-dpi render merely lacked resolution is wrong too. THE NUMBER STAYS, RELABELLED: a document lead BELOW source trust, used for nothing and not to be quoted to Elda as something the catalog prints. Rule 10 says the render is the page; this is the first time the text layer claimed something the page does not, and it will not be the last.
page_observations: THE RICHEST WALL SECTION IN THE BOOK SO FAR, and it brings THREE opening types no wall family has shown: a pull-out door (PE0130, W.15), two STACKED top-hung doors, and horizontally folding doors. H.36, H.48 and H.60 have none of the three.

SUFFIX 04 MEANS SOMETHING ELSE HERE, and this page is the proof the manifest has been warning about. At H.48 and H.60, 04 is a two-module COMPOUND - one door across two carcasses side by side. At H.72 it is TWO STACKED TOP-HUNG DOORS, elevation 36 + 36, one above the other. Same two digits, a horizontal split instead of a vertical one.

AND SUFFIX 30 MEANS TWO THINGS ON ONE PAGE. PE0130 at W.15 is a PULL-OUT door; PE0630 and PE0930 are TWO DOORS. Printed p.228 carries both, seventy lines apart. The type_suffix warning was written from exactly this page and it is worth restating: decode nothing.

THE FIRST WALL UNITS AT d.62. Both boiler housings (PE0501 / PE0601 and PE0600 / PE0900) are 620 deep where every other wall unit in this registry is 350. Depth is per CODE and always was; this is the first time a wall page has used that.

'CUSTOM-SIZED SIDE PANELS' is printed on both boiler housings and on nothing else in the chapter. A stated non-standard property, recorded and not modelled - the envelope is drawn at the catalog width like any other.
THE ONE-DOOR TYPE HAS FOUR WIDTHS HERE - 15, 30, 45, 60. H.48 has two (45, 60), H.60 has three (15, 45, 60) and no 30. Four families, four different width sets for the same type.

THE PUSH-UP TYPE DROPS TO THREE WIDTHS - 60, 90, 120. H.48 and H.60 both list five. It also loses the printed open_leaf geometry note: printed p.229 points at 'Servo Drive mechanism on page 567' rather than giving the oblique figures that p.561 gives for H.60.

wall_pull_out_door.description: Wall unit with pull-out door - 1 door - 1 soft-close pull-out door - no push-pull
wall_pull_out_door.notes: THE FIRST PULL-OUT DOOR IN THE WALL CHAPTER, and the same shape base_pull_out_door has on printed p.36 - one narrow front on a mechanism. The source never calls it rh or lh, so it is not recorded as handed.

front_layout.note: One full-height front carried by a pull-out mechanism, not a swinging leaf. NO hinge_axis and no open_leaf: the travel of this mechanism is not in the catalog, so 70_symbols draws nothing rather than something wrong. Same treatment as base_pull_out_door.

wall_door.description: Wall unit with door - 1 rh or lh door - 1 shelf
wall_door.notes: Four widths, the widest set this type has in any wall family. ONE CODE, BOTH HANDS.

front_layout.note: One door covering the full front, hinged on a vertical edge. Which edge is hinge_side, chosen per order and never guessed.

wall_two_doors.description: Wall unit with doors - 2 doors - 1 shelf
wall_two_doors.notes: TWO widths where H.48 and H.60 each have one, and a W.60 pair of doors is new - the other families start this type at 90.

front_layout.note: Two doors meeting in the middle. Equal widths are a representation assumption consistent with the drawing.

wall_top_hung_doors_stacked.description: Wall unit with top-hung doors - 2 top-hung doors - top door with Push-pull device
wall_top_hung_doors_stacked.notes: TWO DOORS ONE ABOVE THE OTHER, not side by side. The elevation is dimensioned 36 and 36 and the drawing shows two leaves stacked. Only the TOP door carries a Push-pull device, which the page states and nothing derives.

front_layout.note: Two equal fronts, 360 each, summing to the family's 720. NO hinge_axis: the key is a single value and BOTH leaves are top-hung, so setting it would make 70_symbols draw one 720-tall leaf instead of two 360 ones. A figure for a stacked pair is owed in docs/Drawing_Spec_v0.1.md; until it exists nothing is drawn, which is the honest state. The SLABS are correct either way - two of them, which is also what the handle count reads.

wall_push_up_door.description: Wall unit with push-up door - 1 push-up door - 1 shelf - interior Valencia handle - no Push-pull device
wall_push_up_door.notes: Three widths, against five at H.48 and H.60. NO open_leaf geometry recorded: printed p.229 points at 'Servo Drive mechanism on page 567' instead of giving the figures printed p.561 gives for the H.60 oblique system. wall_h60.json's open_leaf is that family's and is NOT carried over - the manifest already notes the two systems differ by height band.

front_layout.note: NO hinge_axis and NO open_leaf. Nothing is drawn for this type in this family until the page that dimensions its mechanism is read.

wall_folding_doors.description: Wall unit with horizontally folding doors - 2 doors - 1 shelf - interior Valencia handle - no Push-pull device
wall_folding_doors.notes: A THIRD OPENING TYPE THIS FAMILY INTRODUCES: the two leaves fold against each other and lift as one. Elevation 36 + 36 like the stacked top-hung type, suffix 89.

front_layout.note: Two equal fronts, 360 each. NO hinge_axis and no mechanism figure: a folding pair moves in a way this catalog has not dimensioned anywhere we have read. Slabs correct, symbol withheld.

wall_compound_2_folding.description: Compound wall unit with horizontally-folding door - 2 doors - 2 shelves - interior Valencia handle - no Push-pull device
wall_compound_2_folding.notes: BOTH SPLITS AT ONCE - two carcass modules side by side AND two folding leaves one above the other. modules_mm carries the first, front_layout the second, and neither describes the other. Suffix 89 again, same as the simple folding type.

finish_restrictions.source_ref: printed p.229 / PDF 231, read off the render
for_all_widths: Unicolor doors (Calacatta Oro, Calacatta Grigio, Cemento Chiaro, Botticino, Quercia Antracite, Noce Sinfonia, Quercia naturale Nodato, Noce Dogale, Travertino, Ardesia Pelda, Ardesia Graphite)
finish_restrictions.note: RECORDED, NOT ENFORCED - M1.6. No asterisks: one width.

front_layout.note: Two equal fronts, 360 each, across both modules.

wall_boiler_housing_door.description: Wall boiler housing - 1 rh/lh door - custom-sized side panels
wall_boiler_housing_door.notes: THE FIRST WALL UNIT AT d.62 in this registry - 620 deep, where every other wall code is 350. It houses a boiler, so it is as deep as a base unit. 'Custom-sized side panels' is printed and recorded; the envelope is still drawn at the catalog width, because the page gives no other number.

front_layout.note: One door covering the full front, hinged on a vertical edge. hinge_side per order.

wall_boiler_housing_two_doors.description: Wall boiler housing - 2 doors - custom-sized side panels
wall_boiler_housing_two_doors.notes: SUFFIX 00 IS A BOILER HOUSING HERE. At H.36, H.48 and H.60 the same 00 is a top-hung door. Three families said one thing and the fourth says another - read the row. Also note W.60 appears in BOTH boiler types, once as one door (PE0601) and once as two (PE0600): the suffix is doing all the work and the width field none of it.

front_layout.note: Two doors meeting in the middle.
